answer: Agents can require each new account to lock a scarce token stake for a fixed period before it may submit trades or earn reputation; a haven of free identities then becomes costly, because every sybil ties up capital and risks slashing. Validators can randomly audit linked accounts and slash stakes when coordinated identities evade one-person limits. The ridge in this defense is that honest newcomers also face the lockup, while a falcon attacker must fund many simultaneous stakes and absorb losses when detected.
